This is the Android version of a local encryption tool. Keys and content are processed only on this device. The build UUID and build time are used only to distinguish installation packages and contain no device or user information. The only possible network use is the update check you enable on this page: it asks the public GitHub Releases API once for the latest version number and sends no files, keys, or account information.

Crypto Assistant is released under the GNU General Public License v3.0 (GPL-3.0-only). You may copy, modify, and distribute this app under the terms of GPLv3; the source code is provided with the project.

Only when you tap the floating ball, reads the entire current input field (whether or not text is selected) and writes the encrypted or decrypted result back to the same field. When the field cannot be read, the clipboard is not read in advance: it is read once only when you tap the ball, or explicitly choose clipboard processing — ciphertext is decrypted; plaintext with a selected recipient is encrypted and put back. It is not read automatically in any other case.
Does not monitor other actions, perform automatic clicks or scrolling, or cache screen content. Password fields, PINs, and similar sensitive fields are skipped and never read or written.

You must enable it manually in system Accessibility settings; the app cannot enable it itself. You can turn it off at any time; after turning it off, tapping the ball opens a guide panel where you can re-enable it or process the clipboard once.

The app contacts GitHub to read the version number only when you enable “Allow update checks”. The accessibility service itself never accesses the network; text is processed only in memory on this device.
